name: ratesonar
description: Dated record of the rates Australian banks and lenders advertise. Read-only MCP tools plus a skill that reports each rate with its date.

interface.longDescription:
RateSonar keeps a daily record of the interest rates that Australian banks and lenders advertise. Each rate carries the date RateSonar recorded it. The record starts on 12 June 2026.

Use RateSonar to:
- Compare current advertised rates across lenders for home loans, savings accounts, term deposits, credit cards, personal loans, car loans and business loans. Filter home loans by owner-occupied or investment, principal-and-interest or interest-only, and variable or fixed. Filter term deposits by term.
- See one product's advertised rate on each recorded day since 12 June 2026, and when it changed.
- Read one product's full published detail: rate tiers, bonus conditions, fees, eligibility and constraints, as the lender published them on a given date.
- List recent rate changes: rises, cuts, new products and withdrawn products, with the size of each move in basis points.
- Read standard series, such as the variable home loan rate minus the RBA cash rate, for each lender and as a market median.
- Place one bank's deposit and loan prices against comparable peers, its own history and the RBA cash rate, with an evidence-checked reading of that position.
- Read dated RBA market curves: bond yields and the RBA's fitted zero, forward and discount curves.

How the data works:
- Most rates come from the product reference data that Australian lenders publish under the Consumer Data Right (CDR). RateSonar also records the RBA cash rate and some lender web pages.
- RateSonar answers from its own stored record. It does not send your question to a lender.
- A day with no record is marked "carried-forward". Spreads and medians are marked "derived". Neither is shown as a new observation.
- RateSonar has no record before 12 June 2026.

Limits:
- RateSonar reports advertised rates. It gives no personal financial advice, does not say which product suits a person, takes no applications and moves no money.
- It covers Australian lenders only. A lender that does not publish CDR product data can be missing.
- Without an API key, series requests return the last 31 days.

Who it is for: people who compare Australian bank products, mortgage brokers, analysts, journalists and researchers who need a dated record of advertised rates.

No sign-in is needed to start. Every tool only reads data.
defaultPrompt: What is the highest 12-month term deposit rate in Australia right now?
Which lenders changed home loan rates in the last 7 days?
How has CBA's standard variable home loan rate changed since June 2026?
